items.title: Scott Yanow interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021
items.q: Here’s what you wrote about Bing Crosby. “He’s probably the first great white male jazz singer who was not a musician.”

ctx.x: That doesn’t mean he’s not good and that doesn’t mean that he didn’t put on an enjoyable show.

Yes. Here’s what you wrote about Bing Crosby. “He’s probably the first great white male jazz singer who was not a musician.” So it begs the question when does a singer get to be considered a musician and most singers I think would object to that statement. I’m not sure most, but a lot of them would. In your mind when does a singer become a musician?

Well I guess I would amend that statement too, because that was written like twenty years ago. I think I would say he was the first white jazz singer, important white jazz singer who was not an instrumentalist. Because singers are generally musicians too, it’s just that some of them are good musicians and some of them are masterful ones. So I would probably amend that statement.
